word:hebrew:H1033.explanation: Beth-Car is the name of a place in Palestine.

word:hebrew:H104.explanation: Iggᵉrâ means a letter or epistle.

word:hebrew:H1068.explanation: This word refers to “mourning,” the expression or period of grief connected with loss. It appears once in the Hebrew Bible, in Genesis 50:4, so its broader range of use cannot be established from repeated examples. Its recorded occurrence is associated with speech about mourning, while the precise force in that verse depends on the surrounding passage. The word therefore points plainly to grief expressed or observed after a loss.

word:hebrew:H1086.explanation: Balah means to become old. It can describe wearing out. It can also describe decay.

word:hebrew:H1121.explanation: Ben means son. Depending on the family relationship, it can also refer broadly to children or descendants.

word:hebrew:H1154.explanation: Beçer means an immature or unripe grape.

word:hebrew:H1235.explanation: Beqa means a beka, or half a shekel by weight.

word:hebrew:H1316.explanation: Bashan is the name of a region east of the Jordan.

word:hebrew:H1491.explanation: Gazah means to cut off or portion out. It can also describe taking someone out.

word:hebrew:H1572.explanation: Gamâ means to absorb. It can describe swallowing something or drinking.

word:hebrew:H1617.explanation: Gera is the name of several Israelites.

word:hebrew:H171.explanation: Aholiab, also rendered Oholiab, is a personal name rather than a Hebrew word with an explicit definition in the available material. It appears five times in the Hebrew Old Testament, all in Exodus, from Exodus 31:6 through Exodus 38:23. The name is associated with passages involving commands and giving, but its precise role in any particular verse requires the surrounding verse text. Its consistent rendering identifies it as a person’s name, not a general description or action.

word:hebrew:H1738.explanation: This word means “if” and functions as a conditional conjunction, introducing a circumstance or condition connected to what follows. It does not describe a person, object, or action by itself; instead, it helps frame a statement as dependent on a particular condition. In the Hebrew Old Testament, it occurs once, in Leviticus 12:2. Its precise force in that verse belongs to the surrounding wording and sentence structure.

word:hebrew:H1763.explanation: Dechal means to fear. It can also describe something formidable or terrifying.

word:hebrew:H1815.explanation: Dᵉlaq means to burn or be burning.

word:hebrew:H1976.explanation: Hallazeh means “this very,” drawing attention to a person being identified as “this man” or “this dreamer.”

word:hebrew:H2036.explanation: Horam is a Hebrew personal name, rendered “Horam.” It identifies one individual rather than expressing a general quality, action, or object. In the Hebrew Old Testament, this name appears once, in Joshua 10:33. Because no descriptive definition is provided for the name, its significance here is its role in identifying the person mentioned, not a separate lexical idea such as a virtue, command, or event.

word:hebrew:H2083.explanation: Zebul is an Israelite personal name.

word:hebrew:H2102.explanation: Zuwd means to seethe. Figuratively, it describes acting insolently, including proudly or presumptuously.

word:hebrew:H2199.explanation: Za'aq means to cry out, especially from anguish or danger. It can also mean to call people together.

word:hebrew:H2230.explanation: Zerem means a gush of water. It can refer to a storm or overflowing water.

word:hebrew:H2292.explanation: Chaggay is the name rendered Haggai, a Hebrew prophet who spoke Yahweh’s message to the people.

word:hebrew:H2465.explanation: Cheled means life or lifetime, especially as a brief, passing span. It can also refer to the transient world.

word:hebrew:H2487.explanation: Chălîyphâh means alternation or change. It can refer to changes of clothing, and it can also refer to courses or turns in a schedule.

word:hebrew:H2559.explanation: Chamaq means to withdraw. It can also mean to go about.

word:hebrew:H2560.explanation: Chamar means to smear or coat with pitch, and can also describe being red or troubled.

word:hebrew:H2641.explanation: Chasrah is an Israelite personal name.

word:hebrew:H2713.explanation: Châqar means to search out or examine closely.

word:hebrew:H2748.explanation: This Hebrew word refers to “magicians,” people identified by that role in the Old Testament narratives. It is used for such figures in Egypt and Babylon, including those summoned to address troubling dreams or signs. The word occurs 11 times in the Hebrew Bible, with most occurrences in Exodus and additional occurrences in Genesis and Daniel. Its use commonly places magicians in spoken encounters where their abilities or interpretations are considered. The precise force in any passage depends on the surrounding context.

word:hebrew:H2814.explanation: Chashah means to hush or keep quiet.

word:hebrew:H2861.explanation: Chăthunnâh means a wedding or espousal.

word:hebrew:H2946.explanation: Taphach means to spread out or extend. It can also describe swaddling a child.

word:hebrew:H298.explanation: “Ahiramites” is a group name referring to people identified as Ahiramites. It appears once in the Hebrew Old Testament, at Numbers 26:38, and functions as a plural designation rather than a description of an action or quality. The word’s precise significance in that verse depends on the surrounding passage, but its basic lexical role is to identify a people or family group by this name.

word:hebrew:H3057.explanation: Jehudijah functions as a Hebrew personal name, identifying a woman in the genealogy recorded in 1 Chronicles 4:18. It is not presented as an action, quality, or object, but as the name by which this person is distinguished in the family record. The word occurs once in the Hebrew Old Testament corpus, so its meaning is limited to this naming use rather than a broad recurring pattern. Its setting is connected with genealogy and family descent.

word:hebrew:H315.explanation: Aharah is a personal name, referring to an individual rather than expressing an action or quality. In the Hebrew Old Testament, it appears once, in 1 Chronicles 8:1, within genealogical material. The name is presented as part of a birth or family line, so its ordinary function is to identify a person in that record. Its precise significance as a name is not defined further in the available biblical evidence.

word:hebrew:H3178.explanation: “Jahleelites” is a plural group name identifying people known by that designation. It functions as a people-name rather than a description of an action, quality, or object. In the Hebrew Old Testament, this word occurs once, in Numbers 26:26, and the same rendering is preserved in both recorded English renderings. Its precise significance in that verse depends on the surrounding passage, but the word itself identifies a particular group of people.

word:hebrew:H3196.explanation: Yayin means fermented wine. It is associated with intoxication and can also be offered to Yahweh as a drink offering.

word:hebrew:H3310.explanation: Japhlet is a personal name, identifying a man rather than expressing an action, quality, or object. In the Hebrew Old Testament, it appears three times, in two verses of 1 Chronicles 7, within genealogical material. The surrounding evidence places the name among people connected with family descent and birth records. Its role is therefore to identify a particular person in Israel’s genealogy, not to convey a general vocabulary meaning.

word:hebrew:H3329.explanation: Yâtsîyʼ means offspring or those who came forth.

word:hebrew:H3488.explanation: Yethib means to sit or dwell. It can also describe being set in a place.

word:hebrew:H3581.explanation: Kôach means vigor, strength, force, or power—the capacity to act or prevail.

word:hebrew:H3611.explanation: Keleb means dog. It can also be used euphemistically for a male prostitute.

word:hebrew:H3664.explanation: Kanas means to collect or gather together. It can also mean to heap up.

word:hebrew:H3725.explanation: This Hebrew word means “atonement,” referring to the appointed means by which wrongdoing is dealt with before God. In the Old Testament, it is used seven times, especially in passages about sacrifices, the altar, appointed holy days, and restoring what has been wrongfully taken. The word therefore points to atonement as a recognized act within worship and reconciliation, rather than merely a private feeling of regret. Its precise force in a particular verse depends on the surrounding passage.

word:hebrew:H3884.explanation: Lûwlê means “if not” or “unless,” marking a condition on which the stated result depends.

word:hebrew:H3949.explanation: Likhi is a Hebrew personal name, rendered “Likhi.” It identifies a person rather than expressing an action, quality, or general idea. In the Hebrew Old Testament, it occurs once, in 1 Chronicles 7:19. Because it is a name, its meaning is not explained by translating it into an ordinary English concept; its function is to identify the individual named in that genealogy.

word:hebrew:H3970.explanation: Ma'avay means desire, expressed as “desires” in a statement about the wicked.

word:hebrew:H4081.explanation: Middin is a proper place name, referring to a location called “Middin.” It is not presented here as an ordinary word describing an action, quality, or object. In the Hebrew Old Testament, it occurs once, in Joshua 15:61, and the English renderings preserve it as “Middin.” Without the surrounding verse text, no further contextual meaning should be assigned to the name. Its significance is therefore chiefly geographic: it identifies one place among the locations named in that passage.

word:hebrew:H4166.explanation: Muwtsaqah means something poured out or cast, especially a metal casting. It can also refer to a cast tube or pipe.

word:hebrew:H4188.explanation: “Mushites” refers to a family or clan associated with Mush, functioning as a group name rather than a description of an action or quality. It appears twice in the Hebrew Old Testament, both times in Numbers. Its setting is genealogical: the term identifies a people-group within recorded family lines. Thus, readers should understand it as the name for members of the Mushite clan or family, not as a general adjective.

word:hebrew:H4225.explanation: This Hebrew word refers to a coupling—the joining or connecting point used to bring separate pieces together. It appears eight times in the Old Testament Hebrew corpus, all in Exodus, in descriptions involving the tabernacle and priestly clothing. Its normal use identifies something that connects parts rather than a person, action, or abstract idea. The repeated use of “coupling” presents the word as a practical term for joining components into one connected arrangement.

word:hebrew:H4311.explanation: Medeba is the name of a place in Palestine.

word:hebrew:H4364.explanation: Makmar means a hunter’s net, or simply a net.

word:hebrew:H4423.explanation: Meleṭ means cement, a smooth clay-like material.

word:hebrew:H445.explanation: Elchanan is the name of an Israelite.

word:hebrew:H4478.explanation: Mân means manna, the bread Yahweh gave Israel to eat.

word:hebrew:H4557.explanation: Miçpâr means a number or count. It can also describe a small number, as in being few in number.

word:hebrew:H4610.explanation: Akrabbim is a Hebrew place-name, identifying a named location rather than describing an action, quality, or person. It is used in Old Testament boundary descriptions and appears six times in the Hebrew corpus, across three verses: Numbers 34:4, Joshua 15:3, and Judges 1:36. The name is rendered “Akrabbim” in the available translations, so its ordinary meaning here is the location’s proper name. Its exact significance in any one passage depends on the surrounding verse and boundary description.

word:hebrew:H4629.explanation: This Hebrew word means “meadows,” referring to open grassy land. It appears once in the Hebrew Old Testament corpus, at Judges 20:33. It functions as a concrete place-word, identifying a kind of landscape rather than a person, action, or quality. Its precise role in Judges 20:33 depends on the surrounding verse and passage, which are needed to explain how the word functions there. The word’s ordinary sense remains a landscape of meadows or open grassy land.

word:hebrew:H4812.explanation: Meraioth is a personal name, rendered “Meraioth.” It identifies a person rather than expressing an action, quality, or general idea. The name appears seven times in the Hebrew Old Testament, especially in genealogical records. In the available genealogical connections, Meraioth is presented as someone associated with being begotten or descended from another person. Its role is therefore to identify an individual within priestly or family lines, while the surrounding verse supplies the person’s exact place in that genealogy.

word:hebrew:H4889.explanation: Mashchiyth means destructive and can refer to destruction. It can also refer to a snare or corruption.

word:hebrew:H4931.explanation: Mishmereth means a charge, duty, or responsibility.

word:hebrew:H4944.explanation: Mashshaq means rapid motion—traversing or running to and fro.

word:hebrew:H500.explanation: Elale or Elaleh is a place east of the Jordan.

word:hebrew:H5028.explanation: Nebat is the personal name of Jeroboam’s father.

word:hebrew:H5073.explanation: This Hebrew noun means “row.” It refers to one organized line or layer of something arranged alongside or above another. The word appears twice in the Hebrew Old Testament, both times within Ezra 6:4, so its recorded use is limited to that passage. Its basic function is to identify an individual arranged unit, rather than an action or quality. The surrounding verse supplies the particular objects being described, while the word itself expresses their orderly arrangement.

word:hebrew:H5150.explanation: Nichûwm means comfort or solace, including comfort restored to mourners. It can also refer to repentings in another context.

word:hebrew:H5169.explanation: Nachats means to be urgent or require haste.

word:hebrew:H5275.explanation: Naal means a sandal or shoe, a piece of footwear worn on the foot. Scripture shows it being worn on the feet and taken off.

word:hebrew:H5297.explanation: Noph is the name of the capital of Upper Egypt.

word:hebrew:H5356.explanation: Niqqayown means clearness in the sense of cleanness or innocency.

word:hebrew:H539.explanation: Aman means to believe or trust. It can describe believing in Yahweh.

word:hebrew:H5406.explanation: Nishtĕvân means an epistle or letter.

word:hebrew:H5767.explanation: Avval means evil in a moral sense. It describes the unrighteous, wicked, or unjust.

word:hebrew:H5785.explanation: Owr means skin. It can also refer to an animal hide used as a tent covering.

word:hebrew:H5819.explanation: Aziza is the name of an Israelite.

word:hebrew:H5820.explanation: Azmaveth is a personal name. It is also the name of a place.

word:hebrew:H5882.explanation: En-Eglajim is the name of a place in Palestine.

word:hebrew:H6076.explanation: Ophel means a tumor. It can also refer to a fort or tower.

word:hebrew:H6115.explanation: ʻôtser means closure or constraint. It is rendered as oppression and can describe a womb as barren.

word:hebrew:H6252.explanation: “Ashtaroth” is a proper name for a named entity referred to in the Hebrew Old Testament. It is not presented here as an ordinary descriptive word with a translated definition. The name occurs 12 times, each in a distinct verse, from Deuteronomy through 1 Chronicles. In several recorded passages, people speak about Ashtaroth and are described in relation to serving it, showing that the name identifies an object of religious devotion rather than a general action or quality. Its precise significance in any one verse depends on that passage’s wording and context.

word:hebrew:H6304.explanation: Peduth means distinction or division. It can also mean redemption.

word:hebrew:H6371.explanation: Pîymâh means obesity, or excessive fatness. In its biblical use, it is rendered “collops” for fat gathered on the flanks.

word:hebrew:H6494.explanation: Pekahiah is a Hebrew personal name, referring to a particular individual rather than expressing an ordinary action, quality, or object. It is rendered “Pekahiah” and appears three times in the Hebrew Old Testament, all in 2 Kings 15. The passages identify this person in connection with his reign and with the people associated with him. Because no separate definition or gloss is provided, the supported meaning is the personal name itself, “Pekahiah,” rather than an expanded interpretation of its parts.

word:hebrew:H6537.explanation: This Hebrew word means “divided,” describing something separated or apportioned into parts. It functions as a description of division rather than naming a person or object. The word occurs three times in the Hebrew Old Testament, all within Daniel 5, appearing in two verses. Its recorded use therefore centers on the idea of something being split or assigned in portions, while the surrounding verse determines exactly what is divided. The English rendering “divided” supports this central meaning.

word:hebrew:H6645.explanation: This Hebrew word is a personal name, rendered “Zibiah,” rather than an ordinary descriptive term. It occurs twice in the Old Testament Hebrew corpus, once in 2 Kings and once in 2 Chronicles. Because no explicit lexical definition is available, its supported meaning here is its identity as the name Zibiah. The two occurrences are in 2 Kings 12:1 and 2 Chronicles 24:1.

word:hebrew:H6700.explanation: Zuriel is a personal name, referring to one individual rather than describing an action, quality, or object. In the Hebrew Old Testament, it occurs once, at Numbers 3:35, and is rendered “Zuriel.” Because it is a proper name, its ordinary biblical function is to identify a person; the name itself does not provide a general teaching or concept apart from the person it names. Its precise significance in that verse depends on the surrounding passage and the person’s role there.

word:hebrew:H6821.explanation: Tsaphad means to adhere or cleave, as skin clings to bones.

word:hebrew:H694.explanation: Arab is a Hebrew place-name, referring to a location named Arab. In the Old Testament Hebrew corpus, it occurs once, in Joshua 15:52, and is rendered “Arab.” Because this word appears only as a name and no broader lexical definition is available here, its basic meaning is the identified place rather than a general action, quality, or description. The surrounding passage supplies the details of that location.

word:hebrew:H6968.explanation: This Hebrew word means “upright,” describing a condition or quality of being upright. It occurs once in the Hebrew Old Testament, at Leviticus 26:13, so its broader scriptural range cannot be established from repeated uses. The word is rendered “upright” in that occurrence. Its precise force in Leviticus 26:13 must be understood from the surrounding verse and passage, rather than from this word alone.

word:hebrew:H7044.explanation: Qalal means brightened, with the sense of being burnished or polished.

word:hebrew:H7112.explanation: Qatsats means to chop off or cut off. It can also describe cutting something into pieces.

word:hebrew:H7189.explanation: Qoshet means equity in the sense of what is true or real, and is rendered as “truth.”

word:hebrew:H7255.explanation: Rôba means a quarter, or a fourth part of something.

word:hebrew:H7303.explanation: The Hebrew word “Rohgah” is a personal name, identifying someone rather than describing an action, quality, or object. It appears twice in the Hebrew Old Testament corpus, both times in 1 Chronicles 7:34. The wording preserves it as a name rather than translating it into an English descriptive meaning, so its significance here is its identity as the person named. Exact details depend on the surrounding verse.

word:hebrew:H737.explanation: Aruchah means a ration of food. It can also refer to an allowance or daily portion provided regularly.

word:hebrew:H7549.explanation: Raqiya means an expanse—the firmament or visible sky. Scripture describes it as dividing the waters and as the place where lights give light on earth.

word:hebrew:H7707.explanation: Shedejur is the name of an Israelite, rendered Shedeur in English.

word:hebrew:H7866.explanation: Shihon is a Hebrew proper name preserved as “Shihon” in the English rendering of its only recorded occurrence. It identifies a named entity in Joshua 19:19, rather than expressing an action, quality, or general idea. Because this word appears only once in the Hebrew corpus and no verse text is available here, its precise significance must be understood from the surrounding passage. This entry therefore supports recognizing Shihon as a name, not assigning it an additional meaning.

word:hebrew:H7888.explanation: Shilonite means an inhabitant of Shiloh.

word:hebrew:H7981.explanation: Shelêt means to rule or bear rule. It can also describe having power, or having mastery over others.

word:hebrew:H8034.explanation: Shem means a name or identifying designation. It can also refer to renown, as Benaiah had a name among three mighty men.

word:hebrew:H8041.explanation: Sama'l means to use the left hand. It can also describe turning or going to the left.

word:hebrew:H8113.explanation: Shimri is a personal name, referring to a particular man rather than expressing a general action, quality, or object. In the Hebrew Old Testament, it appears four times, each time as the name “Shimri.” The references place this name among genealogical records and lists of individuals, but the available text here does not provide enough surrounding context to identify one single person across all four occurrences. Its role is therefore straightforward: it names individuals mentioned in Israel’s historical and genealogical records.

word:hebrew:H8148.explanation: Sheninah means something pointed, such as a taunt. It can also mean a byword.

word:hebrew:H816.explanation: Asham means to be guilty. It can describe someone who has sinned or trespassed against Yahweh.

word:hebrew:H8265.explanation: Saqar means to ogle or blink coquettishly. It can describe a wanton, flirtatious look.

word:hebrew:H8287.explanation: Sharuhen functions as a name, referring to a named place or entity rather than expressing an action, quality, or general idea. In the Hebrew Old Testament, it occurs only once, in Joshua 19:6, and the English rendering is consistently “Sharuhen.” Because no explanatory definition or verse text is available here, the safest meaning is the name itself; its precise historical or contextual significance must come from the surrounding passage.

word:hebrew:H8359.explanation: Shethî means the warp in weaving.

word:hebrew:H8360.explanation: This Hebrew word refers to drinking—the act or practice of taking a drink. It functions as a term describing drinking rather than naming a person or object. In the Hebrew Old Testament, it occurs once, at Esther 1:8, and is rendered “drinking.” Its precise force in that verse belongs to the surrounding sentence, but its basic meaning is the activity of drinking.

word:hebrew:H8409.explanation: Tigrah means inflicted harm or a blow.

word:hebrew:H8430.explanation: Toah is a personal name preserved in the Hebrew Old Testament. It occurs once, in 1 Chronicles 6:34, and is rendered “Toah” in the available English renderings. Because the word appears only as a name and no lexical definition or surrounding verse text is available here, its meaning cannot be expanded beyond identifying the person named. Its role is therefore to distinguish this individual within the biblical record.

word:hebrew:H8492.explanation: Tiyrosh means must or fresh grape juice, or new wine.

word:hebrew:H8636.explanation: Tarbith means an increase or bonus added to the principal. It can also refer to unjust gain.

word:hebrew:H935.explanation: Bo means to go or come. It can describe bringing a person, as when a youngest brother is brought. It can also describe bringing an object, as when the tabernacle was brought to Moses.
